what_was_done: build() now reports a hand-written `const S_* =` found outside the generated:tables and generated:schemas blocks of prelude.js, and one found outside the stamped region of a workflow (_hand_literal_problems). _mapping_problems requires LITERAL_NAMES plus NON_PRELUDE_SCHEMAS (event.schema.json) to equal the set of shipped *.schema.json files. I tested both in a scratch copy. Appending `const S_HANDMADE = {...}` to prelude.js made build --check print 'hand-written schema literal S_HANDMADE'. Deleting the wave-gate-data mapping made it print 'shipped schemas no literal mapping covers ... wave-gate-data.schema.json'. test_build.py pins both guards. One small gap: the regex matches `const` only, so `let S_X =` is not caught.

The code part is fixed. survey requires rounds_used, and wave-gate-data requires all 21 of its properties. The new check relayed_outputs_require_every_property asserts required == properties for survey, checkpoint-result, delivery-data, story-unit, wave-gate-data and pending-output. step-result has an invalid_missing-method fixture. In a scratch copy, the check failed when I removed review_rules from story-unit's required list, retry from pending-output's, rounds_used from survey's, or error from wave-gate-data's; removing method from step-result failed the fixture check and pytest. Still wrong: the finding also asked for VSA-14 to be split, and that was not done. VSA-14 is still recorded as fixed in zz-catchup.json and the ledger. Yet rewrite/spec/schemas/release-result.schema.json still has four untyped properties and no required list, and no ledger entry tracks that remainder. VSA-14's text is also out of date: it says 'survey requires all 19 fields, story-unit requires all 29', while the files now require 20 and 32.

step() builds the identity as prelude-steps.md does: `...(o.pass ? { loop: o.loop || 1, pass: o.pass } : {})`. A result whose method differs from o.method is now unusable and is retried. converge() calls c.arbitrate(open, pass, notes). The spec text in prelude-steps.md and prelude-converge.md matches. A new universal test, 'the amended identity and arbitration', covers three cases: a stub that echoes a foreign method gets 2 calls and then fails; a step given pass alone carries loop 1; and arbitrate receives pass 2 and the dispute note. I re-ran four mutations in scratch, and that test failed each time: dropping the method check, using the old identity form, calling arbitrate(open), and calling arbitrate(open, pass) without the notes.

what_was_done: The prompt text was changed as proposed. relay() now tells the clerk to return JSON.stringify(emptyOf(schema)) with error set, and test 7 checks fragments of that object in the survey and close prompts; reverting to the old {"ok": false} text fails test 7. The failure the finding describes still happens, though, because emptyOf() does not produce a schema-valid object. It fills top-level required fields only, uses '' even where the enum has no '', and leaves nested required members out. I ran a read-only probe against the repository prelude, validating emptyOf(schema) with error set through the harness validator. S_SURVEY fails ('next: missing required property kind'). S_CLOSE fails ('status: "" is not one of [done, partial, needs_human, blocked, failed]'). S_WAVE_GATE fails ('needs: missing required property security'). Only S_DELIVERY and S_GATE pass. I then ran toy-build in a scratch copy with a clerk that does exactly what the prompt says. The harness rejected the survey result ('result of toy-build · survey.next: missing required property "kind"') and the close result (status '' not in the enum). On the platform, the clerk's result is still rejected and retried, so the printed error is still lost. Test 7 checks only text fragments of the prompt and never validates the object. The spec's own emptyOf in prelude-steps.md has the same flaw.

EventLog.build() now refuses any session id that is not a non-empty str (`not isinstance(self.session_id, str) or not self.session_id.strip()`). _fit's slim path slices the string and never calls str() on None. test_session_id_must_be_a_string asserts that EventLog(d, None).build('session.start') raises EventError. Reverting to the old `not str(self.session_id).strip()` in scratch failed exactly that test.

In wave-gate-data, pending is now a required array of story ids, and the state property is gone. wave-script.md now builds its prompt with g.stories.map((u) => u.id).join(', ') to match the story-unit items. The invalid fixture invalid_pending-not-an-array pins the type, and the relay-rule check pins that pending is required. A neighbouring problem, which was already there and is not caused by this fix: holdout_batches has the same item-type mismatch, filed as L2C-catchup-1.

The new check composed_schemas_match_their_sources compares copied properties with their sources, descriptions dropped: checkpoint-result's status, progress, decisions and next against workflow-result; survey.next against workflow-result.next; and every gate-result property against wave-gate-data. Two scratch mutations failed it: adding test_output to gate-result alone ('wave-gate-data.test_output has drifted'), and widening workflow-result.status alone ('checkpoint-result.status has drifted').

All 20 findings named now have an outcome, in outcomes/catchup-fix.json. The code defects the finding named are fixed: converge() passes the dispute notes to arbitrate (P3SEAM-14, which a test pins), toy-story.js no longer passes --subject, and --wait is a global option in long-commands.md (P3SEAM-20). Several of the new outcomes are wrong, however.
- P3SEAM-10 and P3COV-10 are recorded as fixed, with the claim that the scripts 'already did' what the checkpoint signature requires. Both findings are about story.js and wave.js, and those script texts were not changed. topics/story-script.md:55, topics/wave-script.md:37, workflows/story.md:181 and workflows/wave.md:108 still call `vsdd checkpoint <wf> --run <id> --subject <id>`. commands/checkpoint.md gives `vsdd checkpoint <workflow> --run <id> [--outcome failed]`, so a strict parser refuses the standalone story's checkpoint and its lock stays held. The toys also still pass `--outcome ${outcome.status}`, for example done or partial, which the signature does not take, so the claim that the toy matches the signature is also wrong.
- SL1-51 was closed with the evidence that the ingest/map test pins gated()'s stage passthrough. That test reads only the OVERRIDE table. In a scratch copy, removing `stage: o.stage || name` from gated() passed every suite.
- AU-P2-12 is recorded as fixed, but the pointers it names remain in topics/rule-testing.md:11, topics/risks-hooks.md:9, topics/information-walls.md:74, packaging/e2e-story-tier.md:20,37, packaging/proof-greenfield.md:23-24 and commands/status.md:18. Only the four files the triage listed were changed.
